parts.text: In practical terms, these changes will mean less emphasis on technology, with a return to pens and paper. And teachers will

have hard limits on the amount of time they can use technology in lessons, particularly in primary schools.

For some teachers, this may require a complete revamp of their teaching practices. For others, there may be no

difference as they are not using technology much currently.

There is no comprehensive national data on how much time Australian children spend on devices at school.

The rules around tech use have been just as patchy. For example, phone bans are

at state level. Almost everything else has been decided school by school, including whether students bring a laptop and which AI tools they can use.

What does the research say?

The evidence around how much technology is

for learning is also mixed.

Recent international test results suggest 15-year-old students who use devices moderately for learning do better than both heavy users and non-users. But given so few students now go without technology,

argue the comparison with non-users does not tell us anything particularly useful.

Research also suggests raising the bar for the use of educational technologies (which most of the time means screens) makes sense. For decades, we have

sufficient evidence of their positive impact on learning.

For example, a 2015 OECD analysis found countries that had invested heavily in computers for schools saw no appreciable improvement in students’ reading,

or science scores.

Tech can help, but …

That isn’t to say technology never helps. Used for something specific, such as more targeted practice or more precise feedback, it can improve learning.

But there has not been enough onus on those selling technologies to schools to

their positive impact on learning. Instead, implementation decisions are often made on the basis of pilots and word of mouth.

And with the introduction of

AI and AI agents, concerns have moved beyond a lack of evidence around the positive impact of technology on learning to a concern about negative impacts.

Discussions about students using AI to offload their learning have dominated global conversations in education. The main concern is AI use will lead to “
stunting”, where repeated use of the technology can weaken learning and thinking skills.

reading.title: 主旨、理解与信息定位
reading.instruction: 阅读原文后回答 5 道选择题：1 道主旨、1 道内容理解、1 道段落细节、2 道信息定位。段落细节题以题干指定段落为准。

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the overall focus of this article?
options: Making documentaries with scientists can strengthen students' scientific belonging and public trust.
A long-term study links public prekindergarten attendance to better later educational outcomes.
Reducing classroom technology changes school routines and raises questions about digital learning.
Public libraries support communities in many ways and need resources to sustain that work.
questions.explanation: 把标题与全文各段的中心内容连起来判断主旨，避免把同一主题下的其他话题当成本文重点。
questions.evidence: The government now plans to reduce the time students spend on screens and limit AI use at school to improve learning.

questions.prompt: How does the digital-detox position relate to previous classroom practice?
options: It reverses a long trend towards expanding digital technology use.
It continues an unbroken push to add devices everywhere.
It establishes that no classroom has ever used technology.
It concerns only eighteenth-century teaching materials.
questions.explanation: 第 5 段提供了作答依据。正确选项用不同说法表达了文中的信息；请比较范围、数量、因果关系与限定词。
questions.evidence: This position reverses a decades-long trend of expanding the use of digital technologies in Australian classrooms.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is explicitly made in paragraph 18?
options: In a new report, it outlines growing concerns about the use of digital technologies in classrooms.
But there has not been enough onus on those selling technologies to schools to demonstrate their positive impact on learning.
There is no comprehensive national data on how much time Australian children spend on devices at school.
And with the introduction of generative AI and AI agents, concerns have moved beyond a lack of evidence around the positive impact of technology on learning to a concern about negative impacts.
questions.explanation: 定位第 18 段，比较四个选项的具体信息。其余选项来自本文其他段落，并非本段明确陈述的内容。
questions.evidence: There is no comprehensive national data on how much time Australian children spend on devices at school.
